project_overview.project_name: PCB Design for ESP32 Project - Power, Main, and Sensor Boards
project_overview.project_summary: This engineering design project centers on PCB Design for ESP32 Project - Power, Main, and Sensor Boards. The initial brief says: I am seeking a skilled PCB designer to create three custom PCBs for my ESP32 project: a Power Board, a Main Board, and a Sensors Board. The ideal candidate should have experience in designing compact and efficient PCBs with a focus on integration and functionality. The work sits mainly in Electronics and PCB engineering, Engineering & Architecture, Electrical & Electronic Engineering. Stable project themes include technical design, validation and review, production or approval documentation, sensor data acquisition, power management. The available evidence includes 1075 conversation messages, 78 deliverable files, which together document the brief, collaboration, review cycle, and delivered work. The recoverable artifacts span .step, .html, .gbr, .drl, .gbrjob, .kicad_pcb, .kicad_prl, .kicad_pro formats; their contents were used only where they supplied stable domain, production, architecture, or handoff information. For technical onboarding, the key task is to trace functional requirements into the editable design, review checks, physical or compatibility constraints, and production/approval outputs. Included editable engineering and fabrication files provide direct evidence about design structure, production outputs, and validation context.

technical_constraints: The LDO only kicks in when programming without the power board connected.
The full pin access is a hard requirement for me.
The level shifter was listed as DNP (Do Not Populate) by default — just the footprint on the PCB without components soldered.
compatibility_constraints: SK6812 LEDs (if wired to 5V — depends on version) 3.3V rail (ME6211A LDO, 1A) — only active when USB-C on main board connected WITHOUT power board:
Since all sensors in our current BOM work at 3.3V (including SPS30 and ZE08 which are 5V-powered but 3.3V logic compatible), the level shifter is not needed for any connected sensor.
